title: Blackstone Earnings Surge 26% as AI Bets Power Record $1.35 Trillion Empire
excerpt: The world's largest alternative asset manager beat Wall Street estimates handily, with nine of its top 10 best-performing investments linked to artificial intelligence.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • Blackstone's Q2 distributable earnings rose 26% to $1.52 per share, exceeding estimates.
  • Nine of Blackstone's top 10 investments are linked to artificial intelligence.
  • The firm launched a $5 billion joint venture with Google for AI infrastructure.
  • Blackstone's Bagmane office REIT IPO in India was oversubscribed 23.7 times.
  • Total assets under management reached a record $1.35 trillion.

Blackstone Q2 Earnings Report

AI Delivers a Blowout Quarter

Blackstone reported second-quarter distributable earnings of $1.98 billion, or $1.52 per share, on Thursday — a 26% jump from $1.57 billion, or $1.21 per share, a year ago. The result comfortably beat Wall Street's consensus estimate of $1.35 per share.

Total revenue surged 36% year-over-year to $5.04 billion, well above the $3.42 billion analysts had projected. Fee-related earnings climbed 22% to $1.78 billion. Assets under management grew 11% to a record $1.35 trillion, lifted by strong inflows across private equity, real estate, and infrastructure.

The infrastructure investing unit was the standout performer, delivering gross returns of 7.2% — outpacing every other division. The firm's private-equity arm, which holds stakes in SpaceX, Anthropic, and OpenAI, also benefited from years of early AI-related bets. SpaceX went public in June, and both Anthropic and OpenAI could list as early as this year.

A Wall Street Giant Goes All-In on AI

Blackstone disclosed that nine of its 10 best-appreciating investments are linked to AI — a striking concentration that underscores how deeply the firm has woven artificial intelligence into its portfolio. It acquired data center platform QTS for $10 billion in 2021, a deal that now looks prescient as AI-driven demand for computing power soars.

In May, Blackstone committed $5 billion in equity capital to a joint venture with Google that will create a new U.S.-based company offering Google's Tensor Processing Units as compute-as-a-service. The venture, led by longtime Google infrastructure executive Benjamin Treynor Sloss, plans to bring 500 megawatts of capacity online in 2027.

Weeks later, Blackstone's credit and insurance business joined Apollo Global Management and Broadcom in launching the AI XPV Platform, backed by an initial $35 billion. The platform will deploy Broadcom's custom AI chips for frontier labs including Anthropic and OpenAI, targeting more than 20 gigawatts of computing capacity through 2028.

"We are in the early days of what I believe will be the most consequential transformation of industry and markets in a generation."

— Stephen Schwarzman, CEO, Blackstone

Schwarzman said the firm's data center platform could double in size within two years if it executes on its current pipeline. He also acknowledged the risk of "excessive exuberance" in AI investing, noting ongoing discussions with industry leaders and policymakers about job displacement.

Monetization Picks Up, but Credit Headwinds Persist

After a sluggish first quarter hampered by market volatility, Blackstone accelerated its deal activity. Asset monetizations reached $31.8 billion, aided by the sale of a stake in three data centers to Digital Realty and a majority holding in power infrastructure firm Sabre Industries to TPG.

The firm also completed IPOs for advertising technology company Liftoff Mobile and a data center investment vehicle called Blackstone Digital Infrastructure Trust.

Private credit remained a soft spot. The retail flagship Blackstone Private Credit Fund (BCRED) raised $1 billion in the quarter, down from $1.9 billion in Q1 and $3.7 billion a year ago, as concerns about AI disruption to software companies — a major lending target — weighed on individual investor sentiment. Total private credit inflows slowed for a second consecutive quarter to $31 billion.

But President Jon Gray said redemption requests from BCRED have slowed "materially" in July, suggesting the worst of the outflow pressure may be easing.

India's REIT Success
›Bagmane Prime Office REIT raised $360 million.
›IPO was oversubscribed 23.7 times.

India Angle: Bagmane REIT and Data Center Ambitions

The quarter also highlighted Blackstone's deep India footprint. The firm listed its Bagmane Prime Office REIT on Indian exchanges, raising $360 million in what became the most oversubscribed REIT IPO in India's history — 23.7 times. The Bengaluru-based trust owns six Grade A-plus business parks spanning 16.6 million square feet, with tenants including Google, Amazon, Nvidia, and Samsung, and committed occupancy of 98.8%.

For the Indian diaspora and tech workforce, Blackstone's accelerating data center and AI infrastructure buildout carries broader implications. As hyperscale data center development expands globally, India — already a growing hub for data center construction — stands to benefit from the surge in demand for engineering talent, project management, and cloud operations that firms like Blackstone are financing.

What's Next

CFO Michael Chae told analysts that income from investment exits is expected to slow in the coming quarter but return to "robust" levels thereafter. He added that Blackstone expects base management fees to grow at a double-digit pace in 2027.

Despite the strong results, Blackstone's stock has slipped 20% year-to-date through the prior close, roughly in line with its alternative-asset-manager peers, as broader market volatility continues to weigh on the sector. Shares swung in and out of positive territory on Thursday.

Schwarzman offered a parting thought for investors: "Our stock is on sale today. We believe it represents one of the most inexpensive ways to participate in this extraordinary megatrend."
